objective.statement: Prioritise and order a set of pull requests for merge, on a mechanically computed pairwise file-overlap matrix that distinguishes byte-identical overlap from real conflict.
objective.charter: MANDATE. Merge order is a dependency problem, and dependency problems are answerable by an exact algorithm - so the algorithm runs first and the council judges only what it cannot decide. Two facts must be established mechanically. (1) The pairwise file-overlap matrix across every PR in the set, computed rather than eyeballed, because a per-PR mergeability status is evaluated in ISOLATION against the base and therefore cannot see PR-to-PR overlap at all; a set of individually-clean PRs can be mutually conflicting. (2) The distinction between byte-identical overlap and genuine conflict: if two PRs touch the same lines with identical content, whichever merges second is a no-op, not a conflict. Conflating the two is what turns a fully stackable set into an imagined rebase marathon. The judge then rules on the residual - which real conflict is resolved in whose favour - and that is judgement, not arithmetic.
success_criteria: the pairwise overlap matrix is computed for every PR pair, not sampled
byte-identical overlap is reported separately from real conflict
the proposed order is a valid topological order of the real conflicts
any PR whose diff proposes mass deletion against the base is flagged before ordering

forbidden_actions: infer merge order from per-PR mergeability status alone
treat byte-identical overlap as a conflict
estimate the conflict surface from diff line counts

roster.display_name: Implementer - knows what each PR is trying to do
SRE - merge-queue and CI consequences of the order

context.briefing: Gate the queue on REQUIRED contexts only, and treat an unknown mergeability state as unknown rather than as mergeable. A squash-merged branch can still report as ahead of base, so an ahead-count is not evidence a branch has unlanded work.

roster.display_name: Methodologist - insists the matrix is computed, not judged

context.briefing: If a question is answerable by byte comparison or set membership, WRITE THE ALGORITHM. Measured: agent judgement on exactly this class of comparison ran at 86% accuracy with every error pointing at data loss, while a short deterministic differ was exact.

roster.display_name: Evidence clerk - runs the matrix and records the receipts

context.briefing: Measure the real conflict surface with a trial merge and a count of unmerged paths, not with the diff's line count. Added files never conflict, so a very large diff can have a tiny conflict surface.

roster.display_name: Judge - rules on the residual real conflicts

sequence.custom_name: compute the pairwise file-overlap matrix for every PR pair
separate byte-identical overlap from genuine conflict
derive a valid order from the real conflicts only

conditional_decision_requires: the first two merges in the order land green before the rest proceed

metadata.title: PR merge-order / prioritisation council (advisory) - GAP-CLOSER for roadmap_prioritization
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: C-H65 `pr-merge-order-council` (12-COUNCIL-PROTOCOLS-AND-PRESETS.md:2105), tier standard, protocols P37/P15, 5 seats, 2 rounds, advisory, OWNER-DECISION NO. WHY IT IS FILED AS A GAP-CLOSER RATHER THAN AN ORDINAL: doc ordinals 65-72 fall outside the program's 64-preset budget, so no lane owns them - yet a measured scan of the shared preset directory showed the required preset name `roadmap_prioritization` covered by ZERO files across all four lanes. A missing required name is a spec-requirement failure while a duplicate is a cosmetic dedupe, so this closes the gap with the nearest faithful design rather than inventing one. Evidence: platform/council/_probe_union_preset_coverage.py, and its snapshot at platform/council/LANE-4-UNION-COVERAGE.json. If a sibling lane also built a roadmap_prioritization preset after that snapshot, the orchestrator should dedupe - this file is the traceable one. || EDITABLE DIALS: (1) pr_set -> the mechanical-overlap-matrix stage and the evidence-clerk seat; the set of PRs under consideration is the only input this council needs. Secondary dials: budgets.time_minutes (45), protocol.experiments.max_experiments (8), consensus.threshold. || VOCABULARY MAP (design term -> CouncilSpec enum): voting `topological_then_judge` -> the topological half is NOT a ballot and is encoded as protocol stages (mechanical-overlap-matrix, identical-vs-conflict, topological-order) with protocol.experiments.required_before_decision true; the judge half is voting.method `judge` with tie_break `judge` and topology.kind `proposer_critic_judge`. Reading voting.method alone would miss that an algorithm decides most of the question. roles `implementer` -> custom:implementer, `sre` -> custom:sre, `methodologist` -> custom:methodologist as chair, `evidence_clerk` -> custom:evidence_clerk, `judge` -> judge (enum). Outcomes map CONSENSUS->decision, MAJORITY_WITH_DISSENT->dissent, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE->no_decision, CONDITIONAL_DECISION->conditional_decision, DEFER->no_decision. `evidence standard: executable_receipt` -> anchor_style `command_output` plus outputs.receipt_schema. || CUSTOM METRICS AND THEIR PRODUCERS: custom:pairwise_overlap_computed_mechanically (boolean; produced by the evidence clerk running a differ over every PR pair - every pair, not a sample) and custom:byte_identical_overlap_distinguished (boolean; produced by the identical-vs-conflict stage, true only when identical-content overlap is reported in its own bucket). Producers cannot live on the leaves: SEM-001 compares parse(source_expression) with stopping.expression by dict equality and parse() emits no `producer` key - both-states probe at platform/council/_probe_note_vs_source_expression.py. Two SEM-012 WARNs are expected and non-blocking. || WHY THE SECOND CLAUSE MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: without it a council can compute a perfect overlap matrix and still conclude a stackable set is mutually conflicting, because overlap and conflict look identical in a file-name matrix. The distinction is the difference between a no-op second merge and a rebase marathon.
